skill.name: ask-dont-assume
skill.description: Asks focused questions before consequential choices about scope, permissions, privacy, or external changes. Keeps routine, reversible work moving without unnecessary interruptions.
skill.summary: Clarify consequential choices, preserve settled decisions, and review assumptions before material changes.
skill.author: shreyam1008

security_audit.summary: Static analysis reported no findings, so no per-finding verdicts were required. The reviewed skill defines clarification, bounded inspection, and review checkpoints without executable code. No evidence found of prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or unauthorized external actions.

content.value_statement: Unclear requirements can lead AI assistants to make consequential choices without user agreement. This skill guides focused questions, bounded inspection, and review before material changes.
actual_capabilities: Separates known facts, explicit preferences, recommendations, and assumptions.
Guides focused questions when unknowns affect behavior, dependencies, data, permissions, cost, privacy, or external state.
Discourages silent selection of repositories, branches, environments, frameworks, languages, data targets, and push destinations.
Allows safe read-only inspection while awaiting clarification, but prohibits mutation and sensitive data exposure.
Keeps routine, reversible implementation details moving when scope and established conventions remain unchanged.
Calls for one explicit review of decisions, assumptions, side effects, verification, and rollback before material handoffs or external writes.
limitations: Provides behavioral instructions, not technical enforcement of permissions or tool access.
Cannot resolve missing preferences without user input or explicitly delegated choices.
Does not provide scripts, automated tests, deployment tooling, or rollback implementations.
Depends on the assistant recognizing consequential ambiguity and following the workflow.

use_cases.title: Confirm Implementation Scope
use_cases.description: Clarify platform, framework, and dependency choices before implementing a feature with multiple plausible approaches.

use_cases.title: Resolve Product Tradeoffs
use_cases.description: Separate agreed requirements from assumptions and ask focused questions about behavior, privacy, and cost before committing to a direction.

use_cases.title: Confirm External Change Targets
use_cases.description: Resolve ambiguous environments and destinations before publishing or writing externally, then review side effects and rollback expectations.

prompt_templates.title: Clarify a Simple Request
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ask-dont-assume for this task: [task]. Ask a focused question if an unresolved choice materially changes the result.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: clarify a request before consequential action.

prompt_templates.title: Preserve Agreed Requirements
prompt_templates.prompt: Implement [feature] within [agreed scope]. Keep [settled decisions] fixed. Clarify consequential unknowns, but choose routine reversible details yourself.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: maintain momentum without reopening settled choices.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect Before External Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare [change] for [possible environments]. Use safe read-only inspection to clarify ambiguity without exposing sensitive data. Do not mutate until consequential choices are resolved.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: investigate ambiguous targets before external writes.

prompt_templates.title: Handle Delegated Decisions
prompt_templates.prompt: Choose an approach for [task] within [boundaries]. State the choice, evidence, and default before consequential changes. Review assumptions, side effects, verification, and rollback before handoff.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: document delegated decisions and perform a final checkpoint.

output_examples.input: Deploy the update. Either staging or production could be the intended target.
output_examples.output: The deployment target is unresolved. Should I use staging or production? I recommend staging for verification. I will not deploy until you confirm.

output_examples.input: Implement the agreed validation change using the existing framework. Choose helper names yourself.
output_examples.output: I will preserve the agreed scope and existing framework. Helper names are routine, reversible details, so I will choose them without another question.

output_examples.input: You decide whether this change needs a new dependency. Keep maintenance costs low.
output: Choice: use the existing library because it supports the required behavior without another dependency.
Boundary: preserve the agreed behavior and avoid unrelated changes.
Before handoff, I will review remaining assumptions, side effects, verification, and rollback.

best_practices: State settled decisions and permission boundaries before starting the task.
Answer focused questions with the intended target, scope, and relevant tradeoffs.
Delegate routine choices explicitly and confirm consequential assumptions before material handoffs or external writes.
anti_patterns: Treating unclear permissions or deployment targets as approval to proceed.
Requesting confirmation for every formatting choice or helper name.
Reopening settled decisions without new evidence.

faq.question: When should this skill ask a question?
faq.answer: When an unresolved choice materially affects behavior, scope, platform, dependencies, data, permissions, cost, privacy, or external state.

faq.question: Will it interrupt routine implementation work?
faq.answer: It directs the assistant to choose routine, reversible details when they do not change scope or conflict with settled conventions.

faq.question: Can the assistant inspect files while waiting?
faq.answer: Safe read-only inspection is allowed when it tests the ambiguity without committing to a choice or exposing sensitive data. Mutation must wait.

faq.question: What happens when I delegate a decision?
faq.answer: The assistant should state the chosen default and supporting evidence before consequential changes, then document the choice and boundaries in the handoff.

faq.question: What does the review checkpoint cover?
faq.answer: It covers facts, user decisions, remaining assumptions, scope, side effects, verification, rollback, and the next user-visible step before material handoffs or external writes.

faq.question: Does this skill enforce access controls?
faq.answer: No. It guides assistant behavior but does not implement permission checks, sandboxing, or tool restrictions.
